1. What is this product about?
FWD Invest Flexi Elite is a whole of life (till age 100) Regular Premium investment-linked insurance Policy (“ILP”).
It is fully customisable to the unique and evolving needs of each customer. You will be able to choose from a Minimum
Investment Term of either 10 years – (3 flexi) or 10 years – (5 flexi), how much premium you want to pay, the duration of your
premium payment, the currency in which you would like to pay your premium, the number of people covered under the
Policy, and the management of your dividend distribution.
Throughout your Policy term, FWD Invest Flexi Elite will credit different types of bonus Units (Booster Bonus, Annual
Premium Bonus and Contribution Bonus) to your Policy.
To provide support for unexpected events, you are entitled to make 2 penalty-free withdrawals upon the occurrence of
specified life stage events. From Policy Year 3 onwards, we will also waive the applicable premium shortfall charge for up to
4
6 months if you become Involuntarily Unemployed and have stopped paying your Regular Premium.
You will also have access to a range of curated funds from reputable fund managers.
This Policy covers the Person Insured with a Death Benefit.

(i) 105% of the Policy Value; or

withdrawals made).
If more than 1 person is insured under the Policy, we will pay this benefit when the last Person Insured
dies.

3. How much premiums do I have to pay? How do I pay for the premiums?
Regular Premium
Regular Premium for FWD Invest Flexi Elite is payable during the Minimum Investment Term. You also have the option to
continue paying Regular Premium after the Minimum Investment Term and throughout the Policy term.
During the Minimum Investment Term:
i. a premium shortfall charge (where applicable) will be applied if you miss any Regular Premium during the premium
shortfall charge period;
ii. a redemption fee will be applied if you make a partial withdrawal from the initial units account (except for withdrawal
under the Free Partial Withdrawal Benefit); and/or
iii. a surrender charge will be applied if you fully surrender your Policy.

Refund of premium shortfall charge
We will refund 90% of the premium shortfall charge deducted from your Policy, subject to the following conditions:
a. You must pay all missed premiums before the premium shortfall charge period ends;
b. All missed premiums must be repaid in full (no partial repayment of the missed premium); and
c. We will not pay back any missed bonus for the Regular Premium you missed.

Your overall investment return may be impacted. Non-payment of Regular Premium may also lead to your Policy
having insufficient value for the deduction of charges, thereby causing it to lapse.
Top-up premium
At any time, if the Regular Premium has been paid, you can apply to pay a top-up premium. A top-up premium is an
unscheduled, additional premium payment to your Policy.
The minimum amount of each top-up premium is S$3,000 or US$2,250 (whichever is applicable). This amount may change
from time to time.
If we accept your application, we will use the amount of your top-up premium, less a premium charge to buy Units in each
ILP sub-funds that you have chosen or in the funds in your selected investment strategy. These Units will be credited to the
accumulation units account.
Ways to pay your premiums
You can pay your premiums using General Interbank Recurring Order (GIRO) (for Singapore dollar currency Policy only), direct
bank transfer, telegraphic transfer or other modes of payment as updated on our website from time to time. All amounts
payable to and due from us will be calculated and made in the applicable Policy Currency.

6. What are the funds available for selection?
The suite of ILP sub-funds available for your selection is available on our website at w w w. f w d . c o m .sg. For details on the ILP
sub-funds, please refer to the product highlights sheet and fund summary (“fund documents”) of the relevant ILP sub-funds
which form part of this product summary. These fund documents can be found on our website.
The auditor of the ILP sub-funds is Ernst & Young LLP.
The financial year-end of the ILP sub-funds is 31 December. A relevant audit report will be prepared and sent to you by end of
March in the following year. A semi-annual report will be prepared and sent to you by end of August. The latest semi-annual
report or relevant audit report is available on our website.
Past performance is not an indication of future performance of the ILP sub-fund. Investments are subjected to investment and
foreign exchange risks, including the possible loss of the principal amount invested.
Important
When the ILP sub-fund is denominated in a currency different from your Policy Currency, changes in the exchange rate
between the 2 currencies may adversely affect the value of your investment.
7. How are the ILP sub-funds priced?
The pricing per Unit (“Unit Price”) of the ILP sub-funds offered through FWD Invest Flexi Elite is done on a single pricing basis.
The majority of our ILP sub-funds are transacted on a forward pricing basis. This means today’s Unit Price will not be known
2 2
until the next Business Day or a Business Day as determined by the underlying fund manager.
Separately, there are some ILP sub-funds that are transacted on a historical pricing basis. This means that when you buy or sell
these ILP sub-funds, you already know the price which you are transacting at, unlike forward pricing where you will not know.
For more details on the pricing basis of each ILP sub-fund, please refer to the respective underlying fund’s prospectus.
